historical_anchors.assigned_force: Widely used OOB: 1st and 6th Tank Regiments each 37 Type97 + 20 Type95; 14th Tank Regiment 45 Type95 = 159 tanks assigned.
historical_anchors.dated_strength_conflict: Some 8 Dec / 8 Feb OOBs list lower actual counts (e.g. 31+17 and 25+12 in 1st/6th). Treat 159 as assigned establishment-scale and 130-ish as a dated field-strength cross-check, not as an unexplained 29-tank loss.
historical_anchors.Slim_River: About 17 Type97 + 3 Type95 in the spearhead; 4 destroyed and 1 damaged is a commonly repeated local loss anchor.
historical_anchors.Gemas: At least several Japanese tanks were lost/disabled in the Australian ambush; local tactical loss did not change campaign outcome.

branch_opening.note: No Shinhoto back-port. Reliability/QC improves dispatchability but shipping/OOB is unchanged.

first_pass_outcome.Commonwealth_personnel_KWM_delta: +350 to +750 before surrender; POW total essentially unchanged

time_effect.Slim_River: 0-6 hours earlier/cleaner exploitation centered, not a different battle result
time_effect.campaign: 0-18 hours earlier cumulative operational tempo centered; do not move Singapore by several days from vehicle quality alone

system_effect: The largest benefit is infantry/engineer survival and keeping spearhead vehicles present on successive roadblocks, not a dramatic tank-vs-tank kill ratio.
post_campaign_allocation_guard: 1st/14th are later reassigned toward Burma; surviving tanks are not free national reserve on 15 Feb.
